method: Complete candidate survey followed by individual editorial choices and written reasons, applied to the existing complete guide to keep it within 300 quotations. All verified authorized selections included. Priority given to foundational teachings, substantive explanations, necessary qualifications, distinctive applications, narrative examples and thematic breadth across counsel addressed to a life, practical care for family and those in difficulty, work, learning and the use of means, service where one is needed, journeys, permission and changing circumstances, letters as acts of attention, and remembrance, becoming and nearness. Neither citation count nor source order used as a ranking rule. The existing reading arc is retained.

selected.text: and we are awaiting thine arrival
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Kiss thy two dear children on both cheeks on my behalf.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s request that a parent kiss two children on both cheeks on his behalf; a tender instance of personal remembrance.

selected.text: You may travel in whatever direction you deem advisable.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s brief permission to travel in whatever direction the believer deems advisable; freedom in service.

selected.text: His honor Aqa Ali who is present himself doth not need a reply
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh notes that one who is present himself does not need a reply; a light touch on letters.

selected.text: He who visiteth Ukht and Masih in Rayy, it is as though he hath visited Me.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh states that whoever visits Ukht and Masih in Rayy is as though he visited Him; a distinctive honour to named believers.

selected.text: The dhikr you requested should be "Ya Allah'u'l-Mustaghath" eighty-one times
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá specifies a requested dhikr, “Ya Allah’u’l-Mustaghath,” eighty-one times; a historical devotional instruction.

selected.text: Watch over thyself, and over all those who are in thy house, both men and women.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s brief charge to watch over oneself and all who are in one’s house; care for the household in a single line.

selected.text: We sent Munirih - the choice is yours. We gave permission for fifteen days of service.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh leaves the choice to the recipient and grants fifteen days of service; freedom within a permission, closing the section.

selected.text: Do not write anything about these matters to His Honor your father - he cannot handle it.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks a believer not to tell his father about troubling matters he cannot bear; consideration for another’s capacity.

selected.text: Do not write to the emperor; he is proud and preoccupied, and will not take heed at present.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s reported advice not to write to the proud and preoccupied emperor; discernment about timing.

selected.text: The Blessed Beauty knowing his love for hunting told him: 'Don't kill these innocent birds.'
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá recalls Bahá’u’lláh telling a man who loved hunting not to kill innocent birds; a memorable reported instruction.

selected.text: Do not consider me - whether I write or whether I find no opportunity - you must always write.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells a believer to write always, whether or not He finds time to reply; correspondence that does not depend on reply.

selected.text: If thou art able to write the story of Qurratu'l-Ayn as a drama, thou art permitted to write it.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits a believer to write the story of Qurratu’l-Ayn as a drama; a distinctive permission for art.

selected.text: Be at ease and take care of the patient. Do ask after her on My behalf, and also after the others.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s brief instruction to be at ease, take care of the patient and ask after her on His behalf; care for the sick.

selected.text: In these days remain calm and settled in Tehran, and be watchful. The time for presence will come.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bids a believer remain calm and watchful in Tehran, for the time of presence will come; a patient wait.

selected.text: If possible leave immediately for Port Sa'id. Wish send thee India for service. Cable Yazdi. 'Abbas.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s cablegram asking a believer to leave at once for Port Said to be sent to India for service; urgency in a direct instruction.

selected.text: Always write about your circumstances - mention and news are beloved, even if they are already known.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asks a believer always to write of his circumstances, since news is beloved even when already known; letters as acts of attention.

selected.text: If Umm Ahmad wishes to perform the pilgrimage, send your younger son with her to give her peace of mind
selected.reason: The Báb asks that a younger son accompany Umm Ahmad on pilgrimage to give her peace of mind; care within a journey.

selected.text: Beware lest thou overstep the bounds of wisdom, for this is the command of God, the Mighty, the Powerful.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh warns not to overstep the bounds of wisdom; a short, foundational qualification.

selected.text: This is a service specifically entrusted to you - you must carry it out with the utmost joy and fragrance.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tells a believer that a service has been specifically entrusted to him and must be carried out with joy and fragrance; spirit of service.

selected.text: "Will you do this thing?" He asked. "Will you take your heart from this other and give it wholly to God?"
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s reported question, “Will you take your heart from this other and give it wholly to God?”; a direct personal appeal.

selected.text: When security and tranquility are established, God willing, we will invite you to this offered rose garden
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá promises an invitation to this rose garden once security and tranquillity return; a meeting delayed with hope.

selected.text: In spite of this, if anyone has an urgent matter I will see them privately, even if only for a few minutes.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s reported offer to see anyone with an urgent matter privately, even for a few minutes; attention amid crowds.

selected.text: O Badr! Be as a full moon in the love of God, that the handmaidens who are steadfast may be illumined by thee.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image to Badr to be as a full moon in the love of God, illumining the steadfast handmaidens; a name calling for character.

selected.text: As for thy desire to attain the presence - thou art welcome, the door is open and He Who is beseeched responds.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh welcomes a believer’s desire to attain His presence: the door is open; permission freely given.

selected.text: O Hasan! Write the name of thy Lord in the most excellent handwriting. We have manifested it for that purpose.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bids Hasan write the name of his Lord in the most excellent handwriting; the art of calligraphy as devotion.

selected.text: We have ordained for thee to care for him with whom thou wert. Thus hath the matter been decreed in the Tablet.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh ordains that a believer care for the one who was with him; care decreed in a Tablet.

selected.text: Dwell in that land and speak not a word that would cause dissension in Our vicinity or among the people of that land
selected.reason: The Báb directs a believer to dwell in a land and speak no word causing dissension; a personal instruction from the Báb.

selected.text: you may enter into such employment, but you must conduct yourself in such a way as to bring honor to the Cause of God
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá permits an employment on condition that the believer’s conduct bring honour to the Cause; permission with a condition.

selected.text: Either go yourself to Khurasan, or bring that enkindled leaf to Tehran. Neither negligence nor lassitude is permissible.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá offers two options, going to Khurasan or bringing the enkindled leaf to Tehran, but allows neither negligence nor lassitude; choice within obligation.

selected.text: Say: Fear not the turning away of people and their gatherings, and say not that which beseemeth thee not before thy Lord
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bids a believer fear not people’s turning away and say nothing unbefitting before his Lord; courage in a personal letter.

selected.text: Have a seal engraved for me with "'Abdu'l-Baha 'Abbas" - not large but square - in very fine calligraphy and send it to me
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks that a small square seal reading “‘Abdu’l-Bahá ‘Abbás” be engraved in fine calligraphy; a distinctive personal request about art.

selected.text: One must be constrained and cling to wisdom. There are obstacles this year in your honored visit. Let us wait for next year.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá postpones a visit because of obstacles and asks to wait for next year; wisdom about timing.

selected.text: if I say to Mirza Ahmad that he must leave for America today, he must do it immediately and start on the journey without delay
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s reported statement that if He told Mirza Ahmad to leave for America that day he must go immediately; obedience in service.

selected.text: As for the matter of your daughter, if they are known and recognized as Jewish among the people, carry out the law of the Torah.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá directs that if a daughter’s family are recognized as Jewish, the law of the Torah be carried out; a distinctive instruction shaped by circumstances.

selected.text: I have written for thy sake the Message that thou hast requested. Endeavor thou that this Article may appear in the London Times.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá sends a requested message and asks that it be published in the London Times; a letter carrying a public task.

selected.text: go to Canada, stay there for a while, and then return to Japan, for your success is in Japan and it is the cause of your elevation
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá directs a believer to Canada for a while and then back to Japan, where his success lies; service where one is needed.

selected.text: Choose a family surname that indicates nearness [to God], so that this surname may be evidence of closeness to the Divine Threshold
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá advises choosing a family surname that signifies nearness to God; a distinctive instruction about names.

selected.text: Now compose a poem describing this servant's servitude at the Sacred Threshold, that my state may become joyous and my nostrils perfumed.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá playfully asks a poet to compose a poem on His servitude so that His nostrils may be perfumed; a playful exchange about art.

selected.text: Thy visit is accepted and thy name ever mentioned in the presence of Abdul-Baha. I forget thee not for a moment but remember thee always.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells a believer his visit is accepted and that He forgets him not for a moment; the guide’s theme of being remembered.

selected.text: Take heed lest the threats of the wicked frighten thee. Leave them to themselves, awaiting what God hath promised in His perspicuous Book.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bids a believer not be frightened by the threats of the wicked but await what God has promised; courage in remembrance.

selected.text: O Qudsiyyih! Be a sign of sanctification and a banner of holiness, that thou mayest shed abroad upon the world the lights of true chastity
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bids Qudsiyyih be a sign of sanctification and banner of holiness; a name calling for character.

selected.text: The needs of Andalib must be considered. If any funds arrive, assist him moderately according to what is possible on behalf of 'Abdu'l-Baha
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks that Andalib’s needs be met moderately as funds allow; practical assistance within limits.

selected.text: But this is conditioned upon thy taking care of thy health and the providing of whatever conduces to thy comfort, health and prosperity
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá conditions a permission on the believer’s care for his health, comfort and prosperity; health as a condition.

selected.text: Say: O Hasan, We shall soon send that which thou didst desire through the grace of thy Lord. He, verily, is the All-Bountiful, the Generous.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh promises Hasan that what he desired will soon be sent; closes the section on letters.

selected.text: I am in Dublin, sometimes up, sometimes down, in a hotel. Come whenever you wish. Perhaps I will stay for two weeks, then return to Boston.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá writes from Dublin, “sometimes up, sometimes down,” inviting a visit whenever wished; an intimate glimpse of His travels.

selected.text: Hearken unto the call of the Wronged One … Thou playest with the children while the All-Merciful remembereth thee from this exalted Station
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tells a recipient, “Thou playest with the children while the All-Merciful remembereth thee”; a memorable image of being remembered.

selected.text: Tell that dear friend that he is in my thoughts, that he is nurtured by love, that he is full of influence, and that he bears fruit and results
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá sends word that a friend is in his thoughts, nurtured by love and bearing fruit; encouragement through remembrance.

selected.text: As for what you asked about work that would suit you - whatever your father and mother approve for you is beloved in the sight of 'Abdu'l-Baha.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells a young person that whatever work the parents approve is beloved to him; choice of work tied to family consultation.

selected.text: We had written thee permission before, but today therein behooveth restraint and stillness until such time as God shall purify the earth and air
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh withdraws an earlier permission, calling for restraint and stillness until the earth and air are purified; a permission changed by circumstance.

selected.text: O My handmaidens! Consider My mercy … It therefore behooveth you to act in accordance with the requirements of love and to be ever turned toward God
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh calls His handmaidens to consider His mercy and act according to the requirements of love; love as the measure of action.

selected.text: O Nabil, let them come and be content with a stay of a few days, and afterward pass like a breeze over the friends and be the cause of joy to hearts.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asks Nabil to let visitors stay a few days and then pass like a breeze over the friends, gladdening hearts; closes the section on journeys.

selected.text: As commanded, they should adhere to Islam and outwardly hold fast to the resplendent Law. This is better for them, as doth testify His manifest Book.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh directs certain believers to adhere outwardly to Islam and its Law; a historical instruction tied to its circumstances.

selected.text: They must do as they wish; they must solve their own problems; they are grown-ups. We do not like to tell people what they should do in these matters.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá declines to tell grown-ups what to do in their own affairs; a reported conversation that keeps personal freedom visible.

selected.text: You and the guest must act with utmost friendship and kindness, and remind her on My behalf … Then convey Our greetings to the one who was in thy house
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asks a host and guest to act with utmost friendship and kindness; hospitality as an instruction.

selected.text: I pray for thee that thou mayest ever grow in faith and assurance, shine like unto a torch in the assemblies and bestow upon them the light of guidance.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: O Shoghi! Beseech God that thou mayest become a brilliant lamp in the assemblage of the spiritual ones and attain unto the breaths of the All-Merciful.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá bids Shoghi pray to become a brilliant lamp among the spiritual ones; a personal instruction to a named recipient.

selected.text: Q. Now that you have seen me, do you mean all the beautiful things you said in these Tablets? … A. Part is what you are and part is what I hope you will be
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s reported answer that His Tablets describe partly what a person is and partly what He hopes she will be; the guide’s closing word.

selected.text: The Tarbiyat School must instruct the children of Jinab-i-Markar, the teacher, with the utmost kindness, for they are the children of 'Abdu’l-Baha
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá directs the Tarbiyat School to instruct a teacher’s children with the utmost kindness, for they are his children; care extended through an institution.

selected.text: O My leaf and My handmaiden! We beseech God to aid thee to love and protect and turn unto the people of that household. He is the Helper and He is the Kind.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh prays that a handmaiden be aided to love, protect and turn to the people of her household; family care as a prayerful charge.

selected.text: If thou ask my name and title, it is Abdul-Baha and any name beside this is unknown here. Whosoever calleth me by this name, accept from him--otherwise reject.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá declares that his name and title is ‘Abdu’l-Bahá alone and any other should be rejected; names calling for character.

selected.text: O My Leaf! Hearken thou unto My Voice … Be astir upon God's Tree in conformity with thy pleasure and unloose thy tongue in praise of thy Lord amidst all mankind
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bids His Leaf be astir upon God’s Tree and unloose her tongue in praise; a memorable image of a woman’s service.

selected.text: Although at this time, due to wisdom, permission for visits is not being granted, yet the Persian friends are permitted to come, but two by two or three by three.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explains that visits are generally not permitted, yet Persian friends may come two or three at a time; a qualified permission.

selected.text: in multiplicity and, becoming occupied with thoughts of thee, hath taken up pen and ink and letter, that thou mayest know how cherished thou art upon this plane, and how present and renowned, accepted and considered, regarded and remembered thou art in this gathering
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá writes so that a friend may know how cherished, remembered and regarded he is in this gathering; the meaning of being remembered.

selected.text: If some work or occupation should arise that would keep thee busy, well and good; otherwise thy writings are better and more acceptable than any work or occupation.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tells a writer that if no occupation arises his writings are better than any work; the value of the literary vocation.

selected.text: Now in the land of Joseph, the country of Egypt, I have undertaken to write this letter so that you may know you are ever in my thoughts, and I write in my own hand.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá writes from Egypt, the land of Joseph, in His own hand so the recipient may know he is ever in His thoughts; a letter as remembrance.

selected.text: From this talk the purpose is that you should take a ride in the automobile when the weather is good and there is no rain. Mrs. G. must go when the weather is good.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s reported instruction that a pilgrim take an automobile ride in good weather; a homely care for health near the close.

selected.text: Beware lest tribulation prevent thee from the remembrance of the Lord of Names. Remember Him throughout all days, that thy remembrance may endure amongst the worlds.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh, in the Lawh-i-Husayn, warns lest tribulation prevent remembrance of God and bids remembrance throughout all days; steadfast remembrance.

selected.text: Return to thy locality is not permitted in these days. Remain for a time in another place, placing thy trust in God, until God bringeth thee tidings from His presence
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh forbids return home for a time and bids the believer remain elsewhere trusting in God until tidings come; patience under changed circumstances.

selected.text: And whatsoever hath been mentioned in the presence of the Countenance, thou must preserve it in such wise that the hosts of forgetfulness and negligence seize it not.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh charges a believer to preserve what was said in His presence from forgetfulness; counsel kept as a trust.

selected.text: We did not associate with officials and the people while dwelling in the Most Great Prison," He mentioned on that occasion, "but left this difficult task for the Master
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s recollected remark that He left association with officials and people to the Master; closes the section on service.

selected.text: Your letter is present and the Glance of God is fixed upon thee. By My life, this glance is better for thee than whatsoever hath been created in the heavens and earths.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tells a correspondent that the Glance of God fixed on him is better than all creation; the worth of being seen.

selected.text: O maidservant of God! Thy letter hath arrived. Thy dear husband wisheth to complete his education and thou art eager to go to Africa. Now, ye must consult with each other
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: And I counsel you to show love towards the Afnan. You must in all conditions be mindful and seek their good-pleasure. Verily, God is with His patient and sincere servants.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh counsels love toward the Afnán and mindfulness of their good pleasure in all conditions; a family obligation commended with patience.

selected.text: Therefore this letter is for all the divine friends. Make copies and when any individual requests a special letter from you, give this to them and it is specially for them
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks that copies of one letter be given to each who requests a special letter, for it is specially for them; a practical answer to many requests.

selected.text: We have made thee among those who have attained My favors and have entrusted to them the service of the Holy Places. Take what thou art commanded and be of the thankful ones
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tells a believer he has been entrusted with the service of the Holy Places; a personal commission of service.

selected.text: Mansur, if he goes, should recite "I entrust my soul to Thy safekeeping and protection, so protect it, O Protector of all the worlds." It is better if he recites it nine times
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asks that Mansur, if he travels, recite a prayer entrusting his soul to God’s protection, nine times; a historical devotional instruction.

selected.text: I used to write most letters with my own hand, but since three of my fingers became disabled from excessive writing, I was compelled to take a scribe until my hand recovered.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s account that three fingers became disabled from excessive writing, compelling Him to take a scribe; a vivid narrative of His correspondence.

selected.text: Since the day of your departure, no trace or news of you hath come. Forget me not. Ever remember my love for thee. If thou weepest not for my condition, I shall weep for thine.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá writes, “Forget me not … If thou weepest not for my condition, I shall weep for thine”; a memorable expression of personal love.

selected.text: We also, in accordance with our divine obligation, showed him the utmost kindness, even when he requested a letter of recommendation, which we wrote to you. This was our duty.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explains that he showed a man the utmost kindness, even writing a letter of recommendation, as a divine obligation; kindness understood as duty.

selected.text: Now remain in perfect peace and tranquility. God willing, you will be summoned in the hot season. Grieve not at your separation, but be patient and be not of the sorrowful ones.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bids a believer remain in peace, promising a summons in the hot season and counselling patience in separation; a delayed meeting.

selected.text: We counsel you to observe trustworthiness, which God hath made the supreme adornment of the temple of His servants, and to observe religion, without which no deed is acceptable.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh counsels trustworthiness as the supreme adornment and religion without which no deed is acceptable; a foundational statement of character.

selected.text: O Muhammad! Rise to serve God and His Cause, and be a crimson flame unto the enemies of My Most Glorious Beauty and a white light unto the manifestations of My Most Exalted Name
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bids Muhammad be a crimson flame to the enemies and a white light to the faithful; a memorable image of a life of service.

selected.text: Write the first poem on Thursday on green silk with ten marks and keep it with you. Then write the second poem on Tuesday, wash it with water and drink it according to your love
selected.reason: The Báb directs that one poem be written on green silk and kept, and another washed and drunk; a historical devotional practice in its setting.

selected.text: As previously written, you must deal with this through love, kindness, fairness and divine attributes, so that both parties become intoxicated with the wine of justice and fairness
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks that a dispute be met with love, kindness and fairness so both parties are intoxicated with justice; fairness the guide preserves.

selected.text: Regarding what you wrote about traveling to Persia - you came of your own accord and now too you are free to choose. In any case there is no harm in these matters; there is freedom.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tells a traveller that he came of his own accord and is now free to choose; an explicit statement of freedom in personal decisions.

selected.text: In Denver particularly, you must raise the call and guide the friends to the Covenant and Testament. Some souls appear to have doubts and questions - you must deal with them gently
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks a teacher in Denver to guide the friends to the Covenant and deal gently with those who have doubts; gentleness in service.

selected.text: We have heard thy mention and have mentioned thee, and have seen thy turning to Us and have turned toward thee from the precincts of the Prison, as bidden by God, the Lord of lords.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tells a believer, “We have heard thy mention and have mentioned thee,” turning toward him from the Prison; reciprocal remembrance.

selected.text: And thou, follow My counsel and remember the days of My communion after My exile and separation, and be of the patient ones. Then be content with whatsoever God hath ordained for Us
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bids a believer remember the days of communion after His exile and be patient and content; nearness remembered.

selected.text: O Isma'il! Hearken unto the call of the Wronged One. He mentioneth thee even as He mentioned thee before, and desireth naught save thy drawing nigh unto God, the Lord of the worlds.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tells Isma’il that He mentions him again and desires only his drawing nigh to God; remembrance as a call to nearness.

selected.text: We held back Our Pen until the appointed time arrived. Then We loosened its reins and made mention of thee in such wise as cannot be equaled by all the treasures of the earth combined.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tells a believer that He held back His Pen until the appointed time and then mentioned him beyond all earthly treasures; a delayed reply given meaning.

selected.text: Return to thy homeland by God's command and decree, and be not of the hesitating ones. When thou seest thy father, convey unto his face the greetings of this Wronged One, the Peerless.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh orders a believer home without hesitation, to convey His greetings to his father’s face; return as an act of family love.

selected.text: O My Leaf and My Handmaiden, verily We chose thee and accepted thee to serve My Most Great Branch, and this is by My grace which is not equalled by all the treasures of Earth and Heaven.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tells a handmaiden she was chosen to serve the Most Great Branch, a grace beyond all treasures; closes the section on care.

selected.text: Thou hast not the endurance needed for such a trip, especially through the desert. Therefore, rent thou the house which thou hast written about and provide the means of comfort for thyself.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells a correspondent she lacks the endurance for a desert journey and should rent a house and provide for her comfort; care that restrains a plan.

selected.text: When the leaves of fire approach thee, leave them behind thee. Take refuge in God thy Lord, then make mention of Him amongst His handmaidens through verses whereby the worlds are attracted.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bids a handmaiden leave behind her the leaves of fire and take refuge in God; a memorable image of steadfastness.

selected.text: O Hasan! Hearken unto the call of God … When thou arrivest there, visit thy father with what hath been revealed for him from the Ancient Pen. Thus doth the Lord of the peoples command thee
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bids Hasan visit his father with what was revealed for him; remembrance carried into a family.

selected.text: Beware lest thou speak that which may cause harm to the Root of the Tree. Deal with the people, for they are weak and fail to comprehend subtle utterance, and they are in manifest obscurity.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh warns against speech that harms the Root of the Tree and asks that people be met where they are, since they are weak; wisdom in speech.

selected.text: Convey the Most Wondrous, Most Glorious greetings to each and every one of the survivors … Exercise the utmost care and effort regarding their lessons and schoolwork, for they are dear to me
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks that the utmost care be given to the lessons and schoolwork of bereaved survivors, for they are dear to him; care for children in difficulty.

selected.text: my travel and length of stay in each city depends on that city's capacity. Anyone who tries to specify otherwise speaks only for themselves. Wherever there is greater need, I will stay longer
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá states that the length of His stay in each city depends on its capacity and need; a principle behind changing plans.

selected.text: It is not permissible for thee to sever thy connection with Bombay, for thy presence there is necessary, while in the Holy Land there is no work or employment available and the tests are severe.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá forbids severing ties with Bombay, since presence there is necessary and the Holy Land offers no work and severe tests; an instruction to remain.

selected.text: With perfect faith and certitude and firmness in the Cause of the Ancient Beauty, engage in service to the Cause of God. This is certainly better and divine confirmations and success are assured.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá directs a believer to engage in service with faith, certitude and firmness, assuring confirmation; opens the section on service.

selected.text: As soon as letters arrive from here to anywhere, even if brief, write a few lines and send the letters with utmost speed. Never allow any delay, for speed in correspondence has a wonderful effect.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá urges that letters be forwarded with utmost speed, since speed in correspondence has a wonderful effect; a practical counsel on letters.

selected.text: God willing, your honor should remind the people with utmost yearning and attraction, yet never forsake wisdom in any circumstance. Some people are weak, some heedless, and some knowing yet deniers.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asks a teacher to remind people with yearning yet never forsake wisdom, since some are weak, heedless or deniers; service fitted to hearers.

selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá insists that a student pursue medicine with steadfastness and no laxity until skilled; learning as a demanding obligation.

selected.text: O Our Name the Most Truthful! Turn toward the Most Great Scene, detached from the worlds. When thou hearest the Call, leave creation behind thee, turning toward God, the Most High, the Most Great. Hasten and tarry not, that perchance thou mayest see thyself in this glorious Scene … Leave thy son in the house, then travel the path with a single trustworthy companion
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh summons His Name the Most Truthful to hasten toward Him, leaving his son at home and travelling with one trustworthy companion; a detailed summons.

selected.text: Then make mention on My behalf of thy children and those who are with thee, and give them the glad-tidings of this mercy which hath preceded all created things. Say: Hold fast unto the cord of remembrance and praise amidst the concourse of creation, that thereby may be attracted the hearts of those who have been heedless of God when He came with the Kingdom of verses.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asks a believer to give his children glad tidings and to hold fast to remembrance and praise; remembrance carried into a family.

selected.text: Though I am excused by the friends in Khurasan, I am abashed, for during this period of travel I found no time to write a letter or send greetings. Yet with heart and soul I supplicated at the threshold of the Beloved and beseeched His grace and generosity, that He may ever perfume the nostrils of the friends with the fragrance of the rose-garden of divine confirmation.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá is abashed at having sent no letters while travelling yet supplicated for the friends with heart and soul; remembrance beyond writing.

selected.text: O Ali-before-Akbar! When thou hearest that which hath been raised from the direction of the Most Great Scene, turn with thy heart and say: "O Ordainer of destiny and Guide of humanity! I beseech Thee by the Dawning-Place of Thy revelation and the Dayspring of Thy Cause to make me steadfast and upright in Thy love and to make me one who calls out Thy name among Thy heedless servants
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh gives Ali-before-Akbar a prayer to be made steadfast and upright in God’s love; prayer as personal instruction.

selected.text: O servant! We have withheld the Pen from mentioning thy name to protect thee. Behold then the faithfulness of thy Lord Who, despite His imprisonment and tribulations and trials, remembereth thee in a station round which circle the denizens of the Supreme Concourse. By God! This sufficeth thee, wert thou to gaze toward the horizon of the Cause. Be thou grateful and among the thankful ones.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tells a servant that the Pen withheld his name to protect him, yet remembers him in an exalted station; protection and remembrance together.

selected.text: O Mihdi! We have guided thee to the Path and made known to thee the Proof and cast upon thee My Word through which all things have spoken: "The Kingdom is God's, the All-Knowing, the All-Informed." Let not the affairs of the world sadden thee, nor what the oppressors have wrought in the kingdom of creation. Arise to serve the Cause in the name of thy Lord, the All-Conquering, the Almighty
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bids Mihdi let neither the world nor oppressors sadden him and arise to serve; remembrance calling forth action.

selected.text: Your letter arrived, O Jinab-i-Aqa Siyyid Asadu'llah. The friends have surely written about the details of the great gatherings and grand churches. A post also arrived from Iran containing letters addressed to you. Since you had repeatedly given permission to open them, and I also had some private letters within, I opened some and am sending them to you. I have absolutely no time to write.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explains that He opened some of a believer’s letters because he had repeatedly given permission; privacy and permission in correspondence.

selected.text: O Siyyid Mihdi, hearken to the call of the Wronged One from the direction of the Lesser Prison. He wishes to make mention of thee with a mention that shall endure as long as His most beautiful names and most exalted attributes endure. Blessed is he who has found the fragrance of utterance, detached from all else save God, and has held fast to the cord of God's command, the Lord of all worlds
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tells Siyyid Mihdi He wishes to mention him with a mention enduring as long as His names; the lasting worth of being remembered.

selected.text: Although it is difficult and hard for you, arduous and burdensome, yet for the sake of 'Abdu'l-Baha, show kindness and courtesy to Jinab-i-Shukuhi. If you show kindness to those whom you love, that is easy and anyone can do that. But you must, for the sake of God, show consideration and love to souls because of their faith and certitude, even when there is no cause for affection between you.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá asks a believer to show kindness to someone difficult, noting that loving those one loves is easy; a demanding standard of care for the sake of God.

selected.text: Know then that missives and tablets were presented before Us and We found no trace from thee among them, and We became inwardly grieved. Change thy habit, then cast upon the Tablet that which the Spirit casts into thy heart, then present it before Us through a trustworthy messenger. Thus do We teach thee the ways of the Cause that thou mayest act according to it and be possessed of true insight.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh, grieved to find no letter from a believer, bids him change his habit and send what the Spirit casts into his heart; a call to write.

selected.text: Convey to each one that which hath been revealed concerning them, and on My behalf make mention of them with wondrous remembrances and sublime greetings. The press of occupation, as your honor knoweth, hath prevented - otherwise separate letters would have been written and sent to each one. Make special mention of Jinab-i-Khalil, upon him be the glory of God, with remembrance and sublime greeting.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asks that each person be conveyed what was revealed for them, since the press of occupation prevented separate letters; remembrance through an intermediary.

selected.text: Abdu'l-Baha, like the well-known saying, hath no time even for prayers, much less for solving these problems. Since I am confident of your love, good intentions and sincerity, I have therefore referred this matter to your judgment and capability, that you may, God willing, through divine assistance and favor, solve these difficult problems and excuse 'Abdu'l-Baha from involvement in such matters
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá refers difficult problems to a believer’s judgment, confident of his love and sincerity; trust placed in another’s capability.

selected.text: my God! How long wilt Thou leave me in this state of abject lowliness and burning with the fire of separation from Thee, and yet Thou ordainest for those that are near to Thee to ascend to the Highest Summit
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s prayer lamenting His lowliness and the fire of separation; nearness longed for across distance.

selected.text: The Tablets they had requested were sent, numbering five, corresponding to the blessed letter "Ha". As commanded, they should be distributed by lot - that is, after ablutions, place them under a cloth, then draw one Tablet in each person's name and give them to whomever they were intended for. Since the mention of names is not permitted in these days, the names were not written at the top of the Tablets.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh directs that five Tablets be distributed by lot after ablutions, since names could not be mentioned in those days; a distinctive historical practice.

selected.text: Despite this pen being in constant motion day and night and ink flowing continuously, and despite letters from all directions having filled the treasury like that of the forgiven king, with correspondence scattered and strewn from every direction with responses delayed - consider what special attention has been paid to you, that even though no letter has been received from you, a response is being written.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá notes that despite constant writing He replies even though no letter came from the recipient; special attention in a letter.

selected.text: O friends of God! In the religion of God there never was nor is there now any excommunication or accusations of heresy. Disparagement and depreciation are not permitted. Dispute with no one, engage in no conflict, seek not to humiliate anyone, defame no person's name, wish harm to no soul, sully not your tongue with denunciation of any individual, backbite no one, and tear away the veil from no one's deeds.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá, in the Lawh-i-Hizar Bayti, forbids excommunication, disparagement, backbiting and exposing others’ deeds; a necessary qualification on conduct.

selected.text: O Mohsen! Thy letter came to hand and We heard thy call when what was contained therein was presented by the servant in attendance in My Most Great Prison. We have answered thee with a Tablet through which every seated one hath arisen, every hesitant one hath hastened, every tongue-tied one hath spoken, and every heedless one hath turned towards God, the One, the Peerless, the All-Knowing, the All-Informed.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tells Mohsen that His answering Tablet makes the seated arise and the tongue-tied speak; a reply that calls forth action.

selected.text: O 'Abdu'l-Husayn! How blessed is thy name and how auspicious thy smile! Thou bearest the same name as I - thou art 'Abdu'l-Husayn and I am 'Abdu'l-Baha. These two names are in truth one and the same name and title. Thus do we share a name in common
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá delights in a namesake’s smile and says their names ‘Abdu’l-Husayn and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá are in truth one; a tender personal greeting.

selected.text: O Sadiq! We counsel thee at the end of this Tablet to read these verses and preserve them within thyself, that thou mayest be of them that guard. And when thou beholdest in anyone's countenance the radiance of God, the Protector, the Mighty, the Powerful, recite unto him what We have now revealed unto thee, that perchance he may arise from the couches of heedlessness and flee unto a manifest place of security.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bids Sadiq preserve these verses and recite them to anyone whose face shows the radiance of God; remembrance shared.

selected.text: my purpose is that you study the sciences and knowledge, acquire the art of poetry and composition, complete your studies in school, raise the call to the Kingdom, and engage in spreading the lights of truth. You have not yet completed your studies - you must strive until you properly master poetry and composition as you should. At that time, I will specifically summon you to Akka and assign you an important task
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells a young believer to complete his studies and master poetry and composition before an important task; the discipline of language and art.

selected.text: Know that duties are of two kinds: spiritual and physical. The spiritual duties are set forth in the treatise "The Seven Valleys" revealed by the Supreme Pen - they must conduct themselves and progress according to these, so that they may attain the degree of perfection and human reality may be adorned with divine effulgences. The physical duties, along with some spiritual matters, are revealed in the Kitab-i-Aqdas
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá distinguishes spiritual duties set forth in the Seven Valleys from physical duties revealed in the Kitáb-i-Aqdas; frames the relation of counsel and obligation.

selected.text: Follow the course of your journey towards the north, and visit on your way Isfahan, Kashan, Qum, and Tihran. Beseech almighty Providence that He may graciously enable you to attain, in that capital, the seat of true sovereignty, and to enter the mansion of the Beloved
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: O thou who art attracted by the fragrances of the Love of God! I pray for thee and seek help and assistance from the favors of God. Free thyself, by whatever means possible, from Miss Rogess, for her companionship will bring thee into difficulty. Come to Haifa. Go directly to the Household, or to Mirza 'Inayat'u'llah's house, and keep thyself hidden from Miss Rogess. She must not know at all, for if she learns of it she too will come. Suddenly disappear from Beirut and say that thou art going to Egypt
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá directs a believer to leave Beirut quietly and come to Haifa hidden from an unsuitable companion; a vivid personal instruction.

selected.text: By the life of God! His honor Nabil, son of Nabil, upon him be My glory and glory, has been and is in the Most Exalted Prison with the permission, leave and good-pleasure of this Wronged One. However, if his honor Afnan, upon him be My glory and loving-kindness, should send someone to that place for the conduct of affairs, so that the aforementioned gentleman might for a few days repair to these parts by way of recreation, this would be pleasing
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh approves sending a substitute so that Nabil may come for a few days of recreation; rest provided for within service.

selected.text: In most of the revealed Tablets, whether Persian or Arabic, the Pen of the Lord of Creation has, both implicitly and explicitly, forbidden the servants to turn towards this direction, and there has been much emphasis, warning and admonition in this binding commandment from the presence of the Mighty, the Powerful One. You must specifically forbid this and not allow anyone to turn in this direction, for manifest harm lies therein.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh recalls the binding prohibition against turning toward His place and asks that it be enforced, for harm lies therein; an explicit obligation.

selected.text: You should proceed to Karbila and should abide in that holy city, inasmuch as you are destined to behold, with your own eyes, the beauteous countenance of the promised Husayn. As you gaze upon that radiant face, do also remember Me. Convey to Him the expression of My loving devotion. Verily I say, I have entrusted you with a great mission. Beware lest your heart grow faint, lest you forget the glory with which I have invested you.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: a beautiful command. Grieve not over what hath befallen Us, but be patient in God and be of the patient ones. God shall soon exalt thy name in preserved Tablets of glory. Thus have We given thee glad tidings in truth, that thou mayest be of those who rejoice. Then remember on Our behalf Abdullah Baqir and protect him in truth. God shall soon grant him that which shall gladden his heart, for verily He is the Powerful, the Mighty. Then remember thy wife with the most excellent remembrance and glorify her countenance, and likewise the wife of thy brother who is named Hasan. Give them both glad tidings of a mighty paradise. And she whom God hath made thy sister - let her be of the devout
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh comforts a believer and asks him to remember Abdullah Baqir, his wife and his brother’s wife with glad tidings; remembrance extended to a household.

selected.text: My Most Exalted Pen hath testified to thy turning unto God, the Most High, the Most Exalted. This is a testimony that cannot be equaled by the treasures of the world nor by whatsoever the peoples possess. That which hath been ordained for thee by God, the Lord of the worlds, shall erelong be sent down. Rejoice thou in this bounty, then render thanks unto thy Lord, the All-Bountiful
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh assures a believer that the Pen’s testimony to his turning outweighs all treasures and that what is ordained will soon come; what a person may become.

selected.text: thy grievous transgressions and thy grave misdeeds? Consider from the first day when We wrote concerning thee "Fear God, thy Lord" until now - forty months have passed. If thou hadst shown true love and had truly feared God, by Him Who holdeth my soul in His hand, not even a mustard seed's weight would have been diminished from thy glory. Nor did I covet thy dominion even to the extent of a mustard seed, for all of this world and the next compared with recognition of Him is as
selected.reason: The Báb tells Haji Mirza Aqasi that had he shown true love and feared God his glory would not have diminished by a mustard seed; counsel addressed even to an adversary.

selected.text: When ye tire of reading a verse from the Book of God a hundred times, then reduce it by ten and ten until there remaineth but nineteen. This sufficeth you before your Lord in the paths of goodness, if ye be of them that wish to act. Say: Ye draw not nigh unto God by aught as ye do by reading His verses by night and by day, whether ye read them silently within yourselves or proclaim them aloud with your tongues. God hath taught you the measure of guidance in the verses, that ye may attain unto all good. Learn ye from the Book of God that which will
selected.reason: The Báb permits reducing the reading of a verse from a hundred times down to nineteen, since nothing draws near to God like reading His verses; opens the closing section.

selected.text: Therefore, O my God, take me not to task for this grievous error, and leave me not in this state, O Thou in Whose hand is the dominion of might in the most exalted heaven. … Thou knowest, O my God, that this is not due to any pride towards them or independence from them, but rather, O my Beloved, I fear they would be saddened by My sadness and troubled by My trouble. Therefore have I kept myself from meeting them and veiled my face from their sight
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s prayer explaining that He veiled His face from the friends lest they be saddened by His sadness; nearness and distance.

selected.text: From the letter you wrote, it becomes clear that you are compelled to remain in Beirut for some days, whereas swift movement toward Azerbaijan is necessary, as the winds of instability are stirring. However, the dental work must be completed so that there will not be need for repair again later. In any case, strive to complete the work in Beirut. If another skilled physician can be found, well and good; otherwise be patient
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells a believer delayed in Beirut to complete dental work properly before hastening on; care for health weighed against urgency.

selected.text: Should your honour enter that land for a few days with utmost wisdom and without the knowledge of the people, this would be most praiseworthy. However, no writings should be carried, and likewise wherever thou dost reside, acknowledgment before strangers is not permitted. For some time this decree hath flowed from the Most Exalted Pen, for many have attained martyrdom, all sacrificing life and property before the faces of men, yet none have become aware.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh permits a brief, discreet visit to a land without carrying writings or acknowledging the Faith to strangers, recalling the martyrs; safety with its reason.

selected.text: O Rida Quli Kh-A! Today the hosts of God are those who make people aware through deeds, character, wisdom and utterance, and who guide them to the horizon of the Peerless Friend. The visible hosts and manifest ranks hath God, exalted be His glory, entrusted to the manifestations of power, namely the kings. They, through these hosts, protect and safeguard cities and realms. And the friends, through the hosts of wisdom and utterance, conquer hearts and souls.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh contrasts the visible hosts entrusted to kings with the friends’ hosts of wisdom and utterance that conquer hearts; a foundational image of service.

selected.text: O Ismi al-Asdaq! Render thanks for that We called thee to appear before the Divine Presence, caused thee to hear and to behold the effulgences of the countenance of thy Lord, the Most Exalted, the Incomparable, the One, the Great; and sent thee back that thou mightest remind the people of that which thou didst behold and know, and summon them unto the Most Great Steadfastness, lest their feet slip by reason of the clamour of every sinful pretender. O My namesake! Call thou to mind, each day, that whereunto We admonished thee in Our presence. Verily thy Lord, He, in truth, is the All-Knowing, the All-Informed. Upon thee be My glory
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tells Ismi al-Asdaq he was sent back to remind people of what he beheld and to recall each day the admonitions given in His presence; counsel remembered daily.

selected.text: of the Sacred Tree! Your separation has affected us and day by day our longing increases. However, one must obey the command of God and submit to medical opinion. Thus, thou hast undertaken this journey to comply with His command and not for the sake of healing, since healing is in the hand of God, not in the hand of doctors
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá tells a traveller that obeying God and medical opinion is the reason for the journey, since healing is in God’s hand; health and faith reconciled.

selected.text: Were ease and pleasure and freedom from hardships to be considered the highest result of human life, no man could equal in this the cattle. For even when a man becomes the master of great wealth and attains the loftiest honor in the world, a mere cow grazing on the hill-side will by far surpass him in ease and contentment. For the cow enjoys the whole pasture as her sole property, while a man of wealth wrestles with obstacles and hardships and his labors benefit others
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s reported teaching that if ease were life’s highest aim a grazing cow would surpass the wealthy; a memorable image against seeking comfort.

selected.text: Whatever you desire to do, consult with Mr. Parsons, so that he may become infinitely pleased with you. If Mr. Parsons gives his consent you may take a trip to the Orient either this or the next spring. This will become the cause of exceeding rejoicing to the members of the Household of Baha'u'llah. Thus you may spend here a number of days with the utmost joy and fragrance and the susceptibilities of the Kingdom. This is however, conditional upon the consent of Mr. Parsons.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá makes a journey to the Orient conditional on Mr. Parsons’ consent; consultation and consent attached to a permission.

selected.text: O Ahmad! Give praise to God, thy Lord, for having rent asunder the veils from thy face and made Himself known to thee in these days wherein most of the servants remain veiled from Him and have turned back on their heels. Beware lest thou forget thy Lord or take any helper other than Him. Abide beneath the shadow of thy Lord in such wise that the breath of no rejected idolater can cause thee to slip. Turn thy heart toward the direction of God, then seek His help in all matters.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bids Ahmad praise God for rending the veils from his face and to seek His help in all matters; recognition calling for steadfastness.

selected.text: If this is due to the infrequency of this servant's writing, I swear by your precious life that lack of time has so encompassed me that I have no moment even to sigh, let alone write letters one after another. But do not mistake - I am always occupied with your remembrance and familiar with thoughts of you. Do not consider my situation and do not expect continuous replies. Always write, pour forth, and scatter abroad, so that we may see what God will do. Whatever He does is good.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá assures a friend that He is always occupied with his remembrance and asks him to write, pour forth and scatter abroad; remembrance and action.

selected.text: O Salman! We have reared thee through months and years, and preserved thee from the harm of every harmful one, and raised high thy mention between the heavens and the earth. Beware lest thou forget My favor and My manifold mercies upon thee, for My favor hath ever been abundant toward thee. … O Salman! Transgress not the bounds of justice in regard to Me. We have reared thee for this Day. Rend asunder the veils through the sovereignty of thy Lord, the Mighty, the Bestower, and be steadfast in the path
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh reminds Salman that He reared and preserved him for this Day and bids him be steadfast; a life seen in the light of its purpose.

selected.text: according to the command, several souls who are adorned with the ornament of trustworthiness, religiosity, and contentment, and who possess eloquence and utterance, should turn to various regions and with perfect wisdom engage in teaching the Cause. Tablets have been revealed to such an extent that it is impossible to enumerate them. From the Persian and Arabic, whatever is suitable for these days should be gathered and the divine words should be imparted according to the requirements of the station and the souls
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh calls for trustworthy, contented and eloquent souls to teach in various regions, imparting words suited to the souls addressed; qualifications for service.

selected.text: O Herald of the Covenant! Jinab-i-Muhammad Khan, upon him be the Glory of God, has now arrived and attained to circumambulation of the gathering place of the Supreme Concourse, and is now present before this servant. He requests that you remain in Khurasan for some time, and pleads on behalf of the friends. Since they are dear guests, I too am compelled to accept their request. The rest is up to you. The journey to Rasht is also ahead - proceed however you deem advisable and in accordance with wisdom and as circumstances require.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá relays the friends’ plea that a teacher remain in Khurasan, then leaves the decision to his wisdom and circumstances; a request balanced with freedom.

selected.text: Despite physical weakness and inability to endure travel, out of utmost longing to see the faces of the friends, 'Abdu'l-Baha is setting out on a journey to that distant country which is like another world, to cross the great ocean and illuminate his eyes with the sight of the friends' faces. Although this journey will bring me endless hardship, the hope of meeting the friends brings solace to heart and soul. Therefore I am determined to depart in March and make one journey to those regions. I will notify you by telegraph when I depart.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá, despite physical weakness, announces a journey across the ocean out of longing to see the friends; His own travel as love.

selected.text: The correspondence arrived. God willing, a reply shall be submitted. Whatever needs to be sent to your honor shall be sent to that beloved one. The Command is in God's hand, the Lord of the worlds. In these days signs of a cold have appeared in the blessed temperament. If this matter doth not cause delay, replies shall soon be sent. Several letters have also reached this servant from those parts, and have not yet been honored with replies. May that beloved one write replies to those parts and gladden them through the expression of kindness.
selected.reason: The letter reports that signs of a cold may delay replies and asks a believer to gladden others with kind letters; a reply delayed by circumstance.

selected.text: and this matter must, according to the command, remain confidential and reach the known person in sealed form. And this too, if the time is appropriate, for They have said that at certain times some souls are observed to be fearful of certain events. Therefore, consideration of timing is necessary, and furthermore, the known souls have been and are being watched by the enemies who await an occurrence to arise that they might proclaim it. In this case, the protection of known souls is necessary. Blessed are they who conceal and act accordingly
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh requires that a matter reach its recipient sealed and at a fitting time, since known souls are watched by enemies; timing and protection.

selected.text: And concerning what you wrote about Aqa Mirza Asadu'llah, upon him be the Glory of God, that he had sought permission - this was submitted at the Most Holy Court. They said: "Praise be to God, through the wonders of divine bounty he has entered the ocean of attainment and drunk from the cup of meeting. Now let him be occupied with service to the Cause. It would be most loved in the sight of God if, having returned from the Land of Kha, he would proceed to the regions of the Land of Ta, that perchance he might guide the veiled souls and draw them to the highest horizon."
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh, granting a request, asks a returning pilgrim to proceed to the Land of Ta and guide veiled souls; attainment leading to service.

selected.text: In most Tablets We have commanded all to observe wisdom. Nevertheless, in some cities and villages there appeared that which caused the near ones to be struck with terror and the sincere ones with dismay. The first sedition appeared in Iraq, for on the first day of Ashura, in place of sorrow there appeared joy, and in place of silence there arose the sound of singing … Therefore, the requirements of God's loving-kindness and favor - exalted be His glory - are that, as in the past, all should occupy themselves during the days of Ashura with commemorating the tribulation of the Prince of Martyrs, may our souls be a sacrifice for Him, until such time as God shall unveil to His servants the mysteries of His Manifestation and what He hath sent down in His perspicuous Book
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh recounts the sedition caused by rejoicing on ‘Ashura and asks all to commemorate the Prince of Martyrs as before; explains why a direction applies.

selected.text: Regarding your signature, you did not understand the intent. The purpose was not what you thought, rather the intent was that whatever station this servant describes or even desires for himself, you should endorse it - meaning you should mention that same station for this servant in letters and statements. And the station of this servant is 'Abdu'l-Baha. You had somehow thought the intent was about signing your letter - this was absolutely not the purpose.
selected.reason: Corrects a recipient’s misunderstanding of a personal instruction.
